flow.name: axn-term - app starts and restarts without crashing
flow.description: The app must mount its UI on a fresh start and again on the restore path, never falling into the error boundary (a hook after an early return in ShellApp crashed every launch).

step.description: Create temp state: one window, one shell session
First launch
The UI runs a /command line and logged no crash
Close so state is saved
Second launch restores the saved state
The restored UI is alive too
Close again

flow.name: axn-term - closed window does not throttle terminal output
flow.description: After an extra window was opened and closed, a session printing 8 MB must finish about as fast as before (a closed window's dead listener used to slow it from ~1 s to ~35 s). Limit: 8 s, or 5x the baseline on a slow machine (AXN_TERM_FLOOD_MAX_MS overrides 8 s).

step.description: Create temp state: one window, one shell session
Launch axn-term
Print 8 MB with one window open
Open a second window
Close the second window
Print 8 MB again: must stay under the limit
Close axn-term

flow.name: axn-term - pasted line with Enter reaches the shell
flow.description: With a plugin's async line hook active, a pasted "command + newline" arrives as one input chunk. The shell must still get the command and run it once (the chunk used to be swallowed, only the Enter was sent). Real Shift+Insert paste on a private X server; bash without bracketed paste.

step.description: Temp state: bash session plus a sandboxed plugin with an async line hook
Start a private X server
Launch axn-term on the test display
Paste 'echo PASTE_OK_$((40+2))' plus newline into the terminal
Close axn-term and the X server

flow.name: axn-term - Ctrl+S after a failed read keeps the file
flow.description: Open a write-only file with a typed axn-edit: the read fails. Ctrl+S in the editor must not write the empty buffer over the file.

step.description: Temp state: one bash session
Start a private X server
Launch axn-term on the test display
Open an unreadable file, press Ctrl+S, check the file
Close axn-term and the X server

flow.name: axn-term - Git Inspect restore treats bracket paths literally
flow.description: In a repo with app/[id]/page.tsx deleted and app/d/page.tsx edited, "Restore deleted file" on the first must bring it back and leave the edit in the second alone (as a glob pathspec, [id] also matched d). Right-click and menu click at fixed spots of the default 800x600 window.

step.description: Temp state: a shell session in a repo with one deleted and one edited file
Start a private X server
Launch axn-term on the test display
Open Git Inspect with axn-git
Restore app/[id]/page.tsx from its context menu
Close axn-term and the X server
